text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Portugal is well positioned to meet economic targets set for 1997 to join Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), according to a European Commission report.
- Prime Minister Antonio Guterres, speaking during an official visit to Mexico, expressed the need to reinforce cooperation between the European Union and Latin America.
- Small and medium harbours expect to receive 10 billion escudos in infrastructure investment, according to Fernando Garcia, general-director for ports.
- Marconi plans to invest 20 billion escudos in submarine telecommunications cables in Portugal by the end of the century, announced Marconi's president Norberto Fernandes yesterday.
- Tranquilidade Vida life insurance company raised its capital from five to 7.5 billion escudos.
- The ruling Socialist Party (PS) is willing to discuss with the opposition Social Democratic Party limiting the period of the mandate of the Attorney General.
- Portugal Telecom will choose its strategic partner in the telecommunications sector in March 1997.
- Health Minister Maria de Belem Roseira plans to establish direct agreements with chemists to pay for medicines and end the monopoly of the National Association of Chemists.

- Portuguese retailer Jeronimo Martins yesterday bought drinks group Vidago for 15.5 billion escudos. The provisional notification of the public offer to buy (OPA) is due to be delivered to the Financial Markets Committee (CMVM) today.
